svg.title: Consequence-based authority matrix
svg.desc: For each individual operation and immutable subject, assess reversibility, consequence surface, data sensitivity, and authority exercised. The selected tier is not permanent agent clearance, does not accumulate, and grants no blanket authority over later actions. Missing identity, provenance, scope, capability, expiry, retention, or rollback conditions stop the action before it begins. Public or low-sensitivity read-only and simulated work uses Tier zero. Tier one covers reversible local mutation or a restricted-data read only within an expiring least-privilege preapproval bounded by operation, source or target, purpose, scope, capability, retention, and rollback or revocation. Material mutation, restricted-data write or transmission, or a restricted read outside that preapproval requires a Tier two explicit human decision bound to the immutable subject. Legally binding filing or submission, identity-bound attestation, custody transfer, or another explicitly irreversible high-consequence act uses Tier three and remains human-performed. After any permitted operation, missing receipt or live verification marks the result unverified, blocks acceptance and downstream work, and triggers reconciliation or incident handling; it does not retroactively authorize or undo the action.
